sections.title: Purpose and authority
sections.content: The self-hosted acceptance-coordinator-trust-recovery plan repairs Acceptance, Quick Dev, and Knowledge-consumption trust and recovery gaps without modifying the immutable 2026-08-17 historical plan. Lifecycle ownership remains Maintainer for implementation-authorized, Quick Dev for implementation-complete, and Acceptance for acceptance-passed. Bootstrap startup, Knowledge publication, runtime/release actions, and trust signing are not authorized.

sections.title: Implementation slices
sections.content: R0 requires coordinator decisions to derive only from a hash-bound persisted run, action DAG, command registry, and route projection; request-local assertions are rejected. R1 reserves reentrant successor identity before materialization and permits reuse only for byte-identical lineage and bindings. R2 permits a validated same-selection Knowledge refresh successor while requiring reauthorization for selection, authority, scope, resource, policy, contract, command, or test drift. R3 verifies legacy prior-RED evidence only when selector, test bytes, execution fingerprint, and expected failure IDs match. R4 performs a read-only replay of the 2026-08-17 evidence and publishes only new current bindings.

sections.title: Knowledge continuity
sections.content: A verified published or LKG catalog may support degraded execution when catalog staleness or selected non-authority source-byte drift preserves the frozen selection and execution semantics. Failed staging, invalid or tampered LKG data, non-ancestor LKG state, missing required sources, authority-bearing source drift, or selection and scope changes remain blockers. Acceptance and Quick Dev may consume a validated successor context but cannot publish Knowledge authority or rewrite maintainer authorization.

sections.title: Validation and evidence
sections.content: The command registry defines slice GREEN tests, slice terminal checks, full Quick Dev and Acceptance suites, and a terminal-full check. The terminal validator binds the candidate, contract, registry, authority, Knowledge context and freeze, current Skill-input receipt, maintainer authorization, slice receipts, and resume state. Receipts are non-authorizing. Full completion requires all registered checks to pass and final bindings to be present and consistent.

sections.title: Repair constraints
sections.content: The bounded repair addresses terminal argument and predicate compatibility, final receipt bindings, requirement and acceptance traceability, self-hosted authority declarations, historical-plan write protection, and a valid post-repair RED baseline. Pre-existing shared workflow changes lie outside the plan slice write sets and require separate ownership or explicit disposition before plan-ready publication. Repair closure remains absent until targeted validation and maintainer-owned prerequisites complete.

sections.title: Execution boundaries
sections.content: Each slice has explicit allowed production, test, and documentation paths plus protected forbidden paths. R0-R2 carry implementation work and targeted tests; R3 and R4 are regression or replay lanes with no production changes. The terminal predicate is slice-ready for a slice and implementation-complete for the full run. All supplied source content and page coverage are complete for semantic consumption.
